acme_ops: Hey @eli_support — we started seeing corrupted JSON from the API after yesterday's change. Intermittent, ~1-2% of requests.
acme_ops: Example: two objects get concatenated into one response body, breaking our parser.
acme_ops: ```json
{"order": {"id": 42, "status": "ok"}}{"order": {"id": 43, "status": "ok"}}
```
acme_ops: Sometimes fields are duplicated across objects (e.g., items from request A appear inside request B). Happening on both chat and completion endpoints.
eli_support: Ack — sorry about that. Can you paste the exact API call (headers + body) and the model param you're using? Also any request IDs?
acme_ops: We call /v1/generate with structured_output=json_mode, kv_cache=true, batching_window_ms=20. Model: rwd-13b-infer-v1. Sample request_id in logs: req_2026-03-18_8f7a3c.
eli_support: That helps. Two quick asks: 1) can you share a raw response body you received (not our parsed output) and 2) does disabling kv_cache/batching stop it?
acme_ops: Raw body attached earlier (above). We tested briefly: setting batching_window_ms=0 seemed to make it disappear, but that causes latency spikes.
eli_support: Reproduces with batching — noted. Escalating to runtime. @alex_runtime can you jump in? :eyes:
alex_runtime: Looking. If batching + kv_cache are both on there is a known edge where prefix cache reuse can leak fragments between simultaneous streams during interleaved piping.
alex_runtime: Can you dump the request trace for the failing req_id? Need the kernel batch_id and batch sequence.
acme_ops: Trace: batch_id=bn-77, seq=[req_8f7a3c, req_9b3c2f, req_1a2b3c], worker=gpu-04, kv_shard=1
jamie_cs: Customer is on Dedicated, right? Any rate limits or retries we should know about?
acme_ops: Dedicated pool, yes. We do 3 concurrent short requests in burst patterns.
alex_runtime: Possible race: batched streams share an output buffer and the flush boundary for serialized structured output isn't being honored if a previous stream's finalizer runs after the next stream's start. That could concatenate object text.
alex_runtime: Quick repro plan: reproduce with a stress script that sends concurrent structured_output=json_mode requests with small batching_window_ms and kv_cache enabled. If we can repro, tie to worker logs to find where buffer boundaries are not fenced.
tasha_ml: Also worth checking quantization/kernel path differences on gpu-04 — sometimes alternate kernel emits variable chunk boundaries. But concatenation sounds like runtime buffering.
eli_support: For immediate mitigation, can you try toggling: 1) disable kv_cache, 2) set batching_window_ms to 0, or 3) set response_chunking=false (if available) — any of these should avoid the interleaving. Which is least disruptive?
acme_ops: Disabling kv_cache reduced occurrences by 95% in our quick test. Batching=0 also removed it but increased p50 by ~40ms. response_chunking flag not exposed in our integration.
eli_support: Good to know. We'll issue a service advisory recommending temporary kv_cache off for structured JSON workloads in your pool while we investigate.
alex_runtime: I'll start a debug build with extra fence checks on buffer boundaries and run a canary on a single worker. If repro confirmed, we'll ship a fix to ensure stream-level framing is atomic when structured_output is used.
alex_runtime: Could you also provide a sanitized set of prompt/inputs that reliably trigger the issue? Smallest possible case helps.
acme_ops: Will prep a minimal repro and upload now.
acme_ops: Minimal repro: three concurrent requests with prompts that return a single JSON object each. With batching_window_ms=10 and kv_cache=true we see ~1/50 responses corrupted.
eli_support: Thanks. I'll log INF-2026-124 and attach all artifacts. We'll offer a one-month credit for affected tokens while this gets triaged. :white_check_mark:
jamie_cs: Noted for billing. I'll open a support ticket and cc billing.
deploy-bot: deploy finished: runtime-canary/fix-framing-2026-03-18 -> worker=gpu-04 :rocket:
alex_runtime: Canary ran for 3h with extra checks, no reproductions in canary traffic. Patch queued to enforce per-stream framing before merge.
eli_support: We'll coordinate a scheduled patch. ETA for rollout to Dedicated pools: 36-48 hours.
acme_ops: Appreciate the fast turnaround. We'll keep kv_cache disabled for now and monitor.
eli_support: Please ping if you see any new hits. We'll follow up with postmortem when the fix is rolled out. :pray:
